- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥ 0.7) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–2% for next period.
- When sentiment turns bearish (≤ -0.7) or shows strong reversal signals, model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–2% to account for mean reversion.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > true by >5%), model frequently overcorrects in the following period; dampen forecast by 1–3% for 2–3 periods.
- If sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles (e.g., 1, -1, 1, -1), model tends to lag; adjust forecast to align with sentiment direction 1–2 periods ahead.
- For 30-day horizon, model often overestimates in early periods (1–3 days) when sentiment is positive; apply a 0.5–1.5% downward bias to first 3 forecast points.
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (±0.3), model exhibits high variance; use median of recent 5-day history as baseline for correction.
